definitions.explanation: Black clothing worn when attending funerals or memorial services. In Japan, this typically means a black suit or black dress with minimal accessories.

examples.japanese: {喪服|もふく}を{着|き}て{葬儀|そうぎ}に{出|で}た。
examples.english: I wore mourning clothes and attended the funeral.

examples.japanese: {急|きゅう}な{知|し}らせだったので{喪服|もふく}を{用意|ようい}する{時間|じかん}がなかった。
examples.english: It was such sudden news that there was no time to prepare mourning clothes.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}では{喪服|もふく}は{黒|くろ}が{基本|きほん}で、{光|ひか}る{素材|そざい}やアクセサリーは{避|さ}ける。
examples.english: In Japan, mourning clothes are basically black, and shiny materials or accessories are avoided.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{喪服|もふく}を{着|き}る (wear mourning clothes)
・{喪服|もふく}を{用意|ようい}する (prepare mourning clothes)
・{喪服|もふく}に{着替|きが}える (change into mourning clothes)

Japanese mourning attire ({喪服|もふく}) is strictly black. For men, a black suit with a white shirt and black tie; for women, a black dress or suit. {真珠|しんじゅ} (pearls) are the only acceptable accessory. Many adults keep a set of {喪服|もふく} ready at all times for unexpected funerals.
